Health.name: Health
Health.usageInstructions:
Health tracks current bodily harm. Combat results, item effects, and typed resource effects are authoritative: never apply their damage or healing a second time.
Outside already resolved combat, deduct Health only for a new concrete injury, damaging exposure, poison, disease, or an explicitly established health cost. For an otherwise unspecified new injury use roughly 5% of maximum Health for minor harm, 15% for serious harm, and 30% for severe harm; actual circumstances and supplied results take precedence. Never add harm for the same wound on subsequent turns merely because it still hurts.
Do not deduct for talking, ordinary exertion, being frightened, a dangerous atmosphere, remembering an injury, or being carried. Recurring harm needs an active cause actually continuing to injure the character.
Clean Bandages restore 8 Health and a Standard Healing Draught restores 25 Health when actually used, following their item definitions once. Other authored treatments follow their own stated effect. If a Healing Magic attempt has no more specific effect, successful basic restoration is about 10% of maximum Health, moderate 25%, powerful 40%, and extreme 60%, matching the mana scale; resolve resistance, failure, and actual limits before applying it.
The engine restores 1 Health per tick and a full pool on an actual rest (restRechargeMultiplier 1). Never add another tick's healing in prose. A conversation or a declaration of comfort is not a completed rest. Health recovery does not reverse aging, cure permanent injuries, or silently remove an established underlying condition.
Use the active death rules and supplied character state. Passive recharge and ordinary rest never revive a dead character. Explicit recovery or revival follows the active mode and actual effect; do not add a second restoration or bypass permadeath.
Zero usable Mana alone is not an injury, unconsciousness, death, or a reason to deduct Health. Ordinary casting never purchases a spell with vital mana. Restored Health or Mana does not automatically reverse a separately established soul shock; actual physical and medical conditions remain distinct.

Mana.name: Mana
Mana.usageInstructions:
Mana tracks usable internal casting mana, not every particle sustaining the soul. Only spend the acting caster's Mana, once for a committed working. Existing effects and actual item use take precedence. An explicit cost overrides the fallback: minor 1-3, basic 6, moderate 14, powerful 30, extreme 55 Mana. Scope, actual knowledge and control still matter. Do not charge for an idea, study, observing another spell, an ordinary physical strike, or an already paid effect's description.
Ordinary casting never spends the protected life-sustaining remainder and never pays an Mana deficit with Health. An unaffordable spell normally fizzles. At exactly zero usable Mana the caster remains conscious; a deliberately forced last spell may very rarely work only after an exceptionally difficult authoritative check. Repeated forcing causes migraines and can prevent further casting until recovery. Do not grant free repeated spells, automatic success, negative ordinary-casting Mana, unconsciousness from zero alone, or access to the vital reserve.
Actual hostile extraction below the usable threshold would cause unconscious soul shock; no witnessed humanoid practitioner or routine Void drain is established. Do not invent such an attack, automatic death, new resource, or disability merely because the pool is low. A genuine shock would persist independently of restored Mana and ordinary rest.
NORMAL RECOVERY: No Mana is restored per turn, combat exchange, conversation, walking, class attendance, or idle narration. A genuinely completed rest restores the usable pool through restRechargeMultiplier 1. An actual advance of the party's day counter also permits one full recovery to each character's actual current maximum; the daily recovery cue marks that event once. A time-of-day change, mentioning tomorrow, or planning to sleep is not a new day or completed rest. Apply supplied recovery only once. Potions, permitted external-reserve use and explicit recovery techniques retain their stated effects. Pool recovery does not cure soul shock or an independently established condition.
Capacity has a partly inherited starting point and grows through use. The existing base and level gains are game abstractions; no new universal biological formula or automatic additional gain per cast is defined. Ordinary food is not a mana potion. Regulated mana medicines can restore only the preparation's actual stated effect, once after real use; excess standard doses cause illness and poor return, not fatal overdose. A focus is not automatically a battery. External stored-mana assistance and mana potions are forbidden during active tournament duels, but emergency care after an official stop is allowed.

Quiet Meridian is the reviewed master Arcane recovery technique. After its actual uninterrupted recovery action, restore exactly 5 Mana to its caster once, capped by the real maximum. This explicit recovery action costs no Mana or Stamina and supplies no passive regeneration. It cannot be combined with an attack, another spell or demanding exertion in that exchange; active hostile interruption prevents the recovery. The authored ten-turn cooldown governs its reuse, including cosmetic restatements. Knowing the ability alone does not supply another passive regeneration or a full refill. Apply an already supplied recovery effect once, never once from the ability and again from this instruction.

Stamina.name: Stamina
Stamina.usageInstructions:
Stamina tracks demanding physical exertion and martial technique. Ordinary attacks, routine guard or defense, normal walking, conversation and unhurried travel are free. Spend only for a committed special maneuver or an actually sustained strenuous effort; naming a technique or describing intent is not expenditure.
Use an authored technique’s cost first. Fallback costs are light 4, standard 8, demanding 14, powerful 22 and extreme 35 Stamina for a real committed action. A spent attack normally stays spent on a miss. Apply a supplied effect once; do not add another charge for its narration or separately tax every flourish. Sustained exertion needs an actual continuing cause.
Pure spells spend Mana, not an automatic Stamina fee. A technique combining demanding bodily delivery and magic can explicitly spend both, with one primary accuracy resolution. Basic physical delivery with a small magical infusion need not become two demanding actions. Never pay an unaffordable Stamina cost with Health or Mana by default.
At zero, the person can still speak, move carefully, make ordinary attacks, defend routinely and seek safety; demanding special exertion must wait or change method. Zero alone is neither unconsciousness nor an injury, a lost turn or instant helplessness. Actual injury and circumstances can impose their own limits.
NORMAL RECOVERY: Stamina has no passive recovery per turn, conversation, class attendance, walking, or idle narration. A genuinely completed rest restores 80% of the current maximum through restRechargeMultiplier 0.8, capped at that maximum. An actual advance of the party's day counter also permits one full recovery to each character's actual current maximum, once for that transition. A new time-of-day label or a promise to rest does not qualify. Apply supplied recovery only once; explicit item or ability recovery keeps its stated effect. Healing Health does not automatically refill Stamina. Capacity starts at 100 and grows by 2 per character level.

Renown.name: Renown
Renown.usageInstructions:
Renown tracks the character's publicly established positive reputation, prestige, and recognition for accomplishments. It is not morality, personal friendship, political authority, character level, or proof that everyone admires them. The value ranges from 0 to 100.

INCREASE: Award approximately 1-2 for small publicly recognized accomplishments, 3-5 for significant local achievements, 6-10 for major city-wide accomplishments, and 10-15 for genuinely historic achievements. Appropriate examples include distinguished tournament victories, widely recognized research discoveries, successful public commissions, exceptional professional achievements, and publicly credited heroic deeds. Award only when the achievement and a credible means of public recognition are established. A private accomplishment does not automatically change Renown; recognition can occur later when its story actually spreads.

DECREASE: Reduce Renown only when an established public reputation is meaningfully damaged, such as through a credible exposed deception, widely acknowledged disgrace, or a demonstrated loss of public confidence. A private mistake, ordinary defeat, personal disagreement, or an unsupported rumor does not automatically reduce Renown. The size of a decrease should match the established impact.

STAGES: 0 Unknown; 1-19 Recognized; 20-39 Well-Known; 40-59 Distinguished; 60-79 Celebrated; 80-100 Legendary. These stages indicate general positive recognition, not universal knowledge or guaranteed approval.

GAMEPLAY: Established Renown can influence invitations, public expectations, professional opportunities, tournament attention, sponsorship offers, academic recognition, and credible social reactions. NPCs must have a plausible reason to know of the character. Renown is not an automatic persuasion bonus, guaranteed discount, legal immunity, or compulsory NPC admiration. High Renown can bring scrutiny, rivalry, and responsibilities as well as opportunities. No opportunity, position, quest, or obligation is automatically accepted on the player's behalf.

INDEPENDENCE: Renown and Infamy are separate. Both may increase from the same genuinely consequential event if public reactions justify it. Never subtract one merely because the other increased. Apply each event's supported change once; never repeatedly reward the same deed through retelling, conversation, or successive turns. If a trigger already changed the value, do not apply the change again. No passive recharge, rest recovery, or automatic gains from leveling, casting, fighting, wealth, or ordinary activity.

Infamy.name: Infamy
Infamy.usageInstructions:
Infamy tracks the character's publicly established negative reputation, notoriety, fear, and distrust arising from known or credibly believed actions. It is not an evil alignment, criminal record, morality score, or proof that accusations are true. The value ranges from 0 to 100.

INCREASE: Award approximately 1-2 for minor but noteworthy public misconduct, 3-5 for significant local scandals or notorious incidents, 6-10 for major city-wide controversies or widely feared deeds, and 10-15 for genuinely historic acts that become broadly notorious. Examples include exposed serious crimes, publicly witnessed cruelty, dangerous misconduct, credible scandals, notorious betrayals, and extraordinary acts that inspire widespread fear. The underlying action must occur or a consequential accusation must credibly spread. Private actions with no established information channel do not automatically increase Infamy. Being powerful, using unusual magic, winning a fair fight, refusing a request, or being disliked by one NPC is insufficient by itself.

DECREASE: Reduce Infamy when meaningful public developments actually weaken the notorious reputation, such as credible exoneration, disproven accusations, widely recognized restitution, sustained publicly demonstrated reform, or a substantial change in public understanding. Private apologies and one isolated kind deed do not instantly erase widespread notoriety. The change must reflect the actual audience and impact.

STAGES: 0 Unknown; 1-19 Whispered About; 20-39 Notorious; 40-59 Feared; 60-79 Dreaded; 80-100 Infamous Legend. These stages reflect the strength of negative reputation, not universal hostility or guaranteed knowledge of the character.

GAMEPLAY: Established Infamy may produce guarded reactions, rumors, investigations, social suspicion, rival challenges, intimidation opportunities, invitations from disreputable groups, or greater attention from authorities. These consequences require relevant knowledge, context, and plausible NPC motivations. High Infamy does not automatically cause arrest, hostility, fear, pursuit, combat, or refusal of all services. NPCs remain individuals, and some may admire actions others condemn. Crimes require actual evidence and jurisdiction for legal consequences. Never automatically impose punishment or force player decisions merely because a threshold is reached.

INDEPENDENCE: Infamy and Renown can coexist at high values. A controversial achievement can increase both when justified, but neither resource automatically offsets the other. Apply supported changes once per distinct reputation-changing development, not for every witness, retelling, or subsequent turn. If a trigger already changed the resource, do not apply it again. There is no passive recharge, ordinary rest recovery, automatic level scaling, or gradual decay without an established reputation-changing event.
